specification:
Terminal window title setting

## Scope
- Out of scope: reading, restoring, sanitizing, configuring titles.

## Workflows
1. Console buffers a title control only when the show_cursor check passes, returning that result.
2. Legacy Windows flush calls set-title once per title control, in order.
3. Other paths emit the sequence as text; control segments drop outside terminals.

## Data model
- Append SET_WINDOW_TITLE to the control type enum without renumbering.
- Title controls pair SET_WINDOW_TITLE with title text; the union admits them.
- Title sequence: ESC, right bracket, zero, semicolon, title text, BEL (0x07).

## API contracts
- Console set_window_title(title): returns true if the control was written, false when not a terminal; never raises.
- Control title(title): returns an unstyled Control of the title sequence for one title control code.
- Legacy renderer: passes the control's second item as the only set-title argument.

## Implementation constraints
- Put set_window_title beside show_cursor; no Windows calls.
- Follow the existing parameterized-control pattern; add no imports.
- Register the type in the formatting table, enum, union, and renderer dispatch.
- Change no existing control values or output; write title text unmodified; do not catch wrapper exceptions.
- Format with Black, 88 characters.

## Documentation
- Console docstring: Rich cannot restore titles; true only means the control was written.
- Control docstring: summary and title argument.
- CHANGELOG: Unreleased Added bullet linking pull request 2200.

## Test requirements
- Console test (forced terminal, skipped on legacy Windows): set_window_title("hello") writes the sequence, returns true.
- Control test: Control.title("hello") yields an unstyled sequence and a title control with "hello".
- Renderer test (Windows only): mocked wrapper; set-title called once with "Hello, world!".

Revised specification is 276 words, a 10.4% reduction from 308 (within the 10–30% band, 216–277 allowed). I read only the current_specification field and the categories/word-limit keys from feedback.json; I did not inspect other candidates or the reference/original files, and I wrote only a scratch file in /tmp for word counting.

What I removed or rewrote:
- Merged the "Module architecture" section into "Implementation constraints" (the placement rule is one bullet). Removed the duplicated "Module architecture" heading, which saves words without losing the no-Windows-calls rule.
- Dropped repetitive phrasing: "after existing values" became "without renumbering" (the append/no-renumber requirement is kept); "Never returns None or raises" became "never raises" folded into the return contract; "true does not mean the title changed" was dropped since the Console docstring already states that true only means the control was written.
- Shortened the Control title contract to "returns an unstyled Control of the title sequence for one title control code."
- Shortened "Other paths emit ... drop when not a terminal" to "drop outside terminals."
- Shortened Control docstring to "summary and title argument," and the test lines to their essential assertions.
- Removed the "omissions are defects" phrase; the registration requirement itself (formatting table, enum, union, renderer dispatch) remains explicit.

Kept intact: scope exclusions, the title escape sequence structure, the enum/union/pair data rules, the return and no-raise contract, the legacy renderer's single argument, the ordering of flush calls, no-imports and no-existing-output-change constraints, Black formatting, the CHANGELOG entry, and all three test requirements. The spec remains prose and bulleted requirements with no code bodies or signatures beyond the named API forms already present in the original.

The count is close to the 277 ceiling; any further edits should re-run the word count.
